short_description: Non-destructive testing of blade laminates by ultrasonic or thermographic probes in contact with the surface.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Crawler and suspended robots have carried ultrasonic probes in trials, but contact NDT on an installed blade needs consistent coupling on a curved surface at height, which no vendor sells routinely. It is a pilot task whose demand is real because subsurface defects are what visual inspection misses.
advance_criteria: A vendor offering NDT as a priced service, not a trial
Repeatable coupling quality demonstrated across blade types
Owner acceptance of robotic NDT reports for repair decisions

incumbent_process.text: Technician-held probes from rope access, or blade removal for inspection.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Contact NDT is rarely done on installed blades because of access cost.

approaches.short_description: A robot that adheres to and walks along the blade surface, carrying inspection or repair tooling directly to the defect.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: BladeBUG-type crawlers have completed offshore trials and demonstrated inspection and light repair on live turbines, but there is no repeated paid deployment programme and deployment to the blade still needs a crew at the nacelle. The approach has the best contact geometry and the worst logistics.
advance_criteria: Paid campaigns across multiple wind farms in a season
Repair quality accepted by an OEM or ISP under contract

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Owners of ageing fleets are the demand source.
